question: Should NATO escort ships in the Black Sea, yes or no?

lines.text: Bulgaria has called in Russia's ambassador after drones hit two ships off its coast.
Prime Minister Rumen Radev says one sank, 17 nautical miles east of Krapets.
The other, the Chelsea 3, was hit by three drones.
BTA says it is Ukrainian-owned and Malta-flagged.
Border Police rescued all 15 crew, seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis, and took them to Varna.
Radev calls it absolutely unacceptable, but says there is no clear evidence against anyone.
He says logic indicates the result is in favour of the Russian Federation.

scene.quote: the result is in favour of the Russian Federation

lines.text: In Sofia, he has now held talks with Russia's ambassador, Eleonora Mitrofanova.
It is the second attack in a week.
On the sixth of October, the Alfa Watan sank further out to sea.
The EU's Ursula von der Leyen calls the Black Sea another front of escalation.
lines.note: von der Leyen on X, via Al Jazeera

lines.text: NATO's Mark Rutte spoke to Radev, and says NATO will adjust its defences as needed.
Should NATO escort ships in the Black Sea, yes or no?

caption: Bulgaria, Black Sea, Russia: drones have hit two ships off Bulgaria's coast and one has sunk, the second attack in a week. PM Rumen Radev says there is no clear evidence against anyone, but logic points to Russia benefiting, and he has called in Russia's ambassador. Should NATO escort ships in the Black Sea, yes or no?
notes_full: First reported 13 Oct about 01:30 to 02:00 UTC (Radev Facebook, BTA, Fakti, AP 02:07, Maritime Executive 02:55, Reuters 05:27), then BBC, Al Jazeera, Euronews, Politico, Bloomberg; about 9h old at delivery

Removal-risk: events and statements; attribution only as Radev's own words (no clear evidence, logic favours Russia); no missing-crew count or toll; no future-attack framing; neutral yes/no; 6 Oct Bulgaria video was FYP-restricted, so this one is diplomacy-led and toll-free
